Moderna Museet

Skeppsholmen

Sweden’s museum of modern and contemporary art, on the island of Skeppsholmen in central Stockholm.

Skansen

Djurgården

The world’s oldest open-air museum, founded in 1891. Wander through historic houses and farms from across Sweden, and meet Nordic animals such as moose, bears and seals.

Djurgården

Eat, fika & drinks

Where to go

Fika

Looking for a break between sessions? Fika is the Swedish coffee break: a coffee and a cinnamon bun with friends or colleagues.

★ Offer · 10% off fika

Älvsjö Konditori & Bageri

Älvsjö

Looking for a fika spot just minutes from Stockholmsmässan? This local bakery and café is less than a 10-minute walk from the venue, perfect for a coffee and a fresh pastry between sessions. Open weekdays 07:00–18:00.

Delegate offer: show your conference badge for 10% off the fika of your choice.

Visit website

Vete-Katten

A Stockholm institution, founded in 1928 by Ester Nordhammar at a time when women-run businesses were rare. The name is a Swedish pun: asked what she would call her shop, she reportedly answered “det vete katten”, meaning “the cat knows”. Step inside for counters full of cinnamon buns, cardamom buns and the classic green princess cake.

Visit website

Café Pascal

Vasastan

A favourite with Stockholm’s coffee crowd, named Café of the Year 2021 by White Guide. Don’t leave without trying the cardamom bun.

Visit website

Swedish food

Feeling hungry? Try the classics: meatballs with lingonberries and mashed potatoes, or pickled herring and gravlax.

★ Offer · 10% off food

Fotografiska Restaurant

Södermalm

Award-winning, largely plant-based seasonal cooking at the Fotografiska photography museum, with one of the best waterfront views in Stockholm.

Delegate offer: show your conference badge for 10% off food in the restaurant.

Visit website
★ Offer · 10% off

Meatballs for the People

Södermalm

Sweden’s first meatball restaurant, serving handmade, organic meatballs, from classic beef to moose, reindeer and wild boar. Near Nytorget.

Delegate offer: 10% off food and drinks, 9–15 November. Show your conference badge or ticket.

Book a table

Pelikan

Södermalm

A classic beer hall serving Swedish home cooking in a grand 1904 dining hall. The Pelikan name goes back to a cellar tavern opened in 1664, and a century ago this was where wholesalers and hauliers gathered after their deliveries. Come for meatballs, herring and a glass of snaps.

Visit website

Drinks

Experience traditional Swedish drinking culture. Aquavit is often served at celebrations, typically after a “snapsvisa”, a traditional drinking song.

Röda Huset (The Red House)

Sergels torg

Not ready to call it a night after the Networking Dinner? Röda Huset, one of The World’s 50 Best Bars, is just a short walk away. This award-winning cocktail bar ranked No. 35 in 2025, and is open Tuesday to Thursday 17:00–00:00.

Visit website

Pharmarium

Gamla stan

Cocktails with a prescription. This bar on Stortorget sits where one of Sweden’s very first pharmacies opened in 1575, back when the shelves held “unicorn horn” and powdered gemstones. Today the elixirs come in a glass. Open Wednesday and Thursday until midnight.

Visit website

Tjoget

Hornstull, Södermalm

A Hornstull favourite since 2012, with a cocktail bar, beer café and Mediterranean small-plates restaurant under one roof. Named Best Bar in Sweden 2026, it’s all about relaxed, very drinkable cocktails (try the signature Beets by Tjoget), with local DJs as the night goes on.

Visit website
